tonight.headline: The lineup is set — claim Metcalf before 01:00 and you are a 71% favourite
body: Bad news first: Terry McLaurin's MRI came back this afternoon — season-ending knee surgery (Yahoo 19:07Z). He is a dead roster spot in a league with no IR slot.

The three bye swaps from this morning are made: Love, Gordon and Jefferson are in, and the lineup as set is the projection lineup, 129.5 against JuiceJam's 90.2. The one thing left is tonight's claim — Metcalf for McLaurin, before waivers process at 01:00 CDMX.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: JuiceJam start James Cook on a bye and carry Jacobs and Montgomery on the bench. They need a 40-point swing; a Warren or Jefferson injury report this week is the only thing on your side that moves it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: JuiceJam replacing Cook with Josh Jacobs if Green Bay clear him (Packers undecided, DK Network 20 Oct) — about 12.7 back on their side.

doFirst.title: Claim DK Metcalf
doFirst.subtitle: Drop Terry McLaurin — Tuesday's MRI confirmed season-ending surgery, and Chem has no IR slot.

case.label: The clock
case.body: This is the last brief before claims lock: waivers process at 07:00 UTC, 01:00 Wednesday in Mexico City. Wednesday morning's brief is too late.

case.label: The player
case.body: Pittsburgh's WR1: 15 targets in Week 6 (archive), and the Week 5 dip was an illness (Athlon 18 Oct). Pittman is on IR until at least Week 10 (DK Network 20 Oct) and Roman Wilson went on IR at the weekend (Steelers Depot 20 Oct); Metcalf and Germie Bernard are the starters on Tuesday's depth chart.

case.label: The drop
case.body: McLaurin needs season-ending knee surgery after Tuesday's MRI (Yahoo 20 Oct, 19:07Z). The morning's only reason to wait — a short-term diagnosis — is gone. He is still 85.8% rostered; the market has not caught up.

case.label: The cost
case.body: Priority resets weekly in Chem, so nothing lasting. Metcalf does not start this week (14.9 sits below every started receiver; the lowest, Wilson at 15.1, is a coin flip the projection gives Wilson); he is the receiver depth McLaurin was, from Week 8.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Metcalf draws under six targets in two of Weeks 7-9 with Pittman still out (archive).

doFirst.sources: Yahoo 20 Oct · Athlon 18 Oct · Steelers Depot 20 Oct · DK Network 20 Oct

whatWentWrong.title: McLaurin's season is over and he holds a roster spot
whatWentWrong.lead: Tuesday's MRI: season-ending knee surgery. Chem has no IR slot.

case.label: What happened
case.body: He left Monday night in an air cast after one catch; the MRI on Tuesday showed he needs season-ending surgery (Yahoo 20 Oct, 19:07Z).

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The spot pays for the Metcalf claim above, tonight. The morning's condition for cancelling the claim — a short-term diagnosis — cannot fire now.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Washington put him on a designated-to-return IR track inside eight weeks — not what the reporting says.

whatWentWrong.title: Week 6 was won with 11.0 left on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: Kamara's 14.9 sat behind Allgeier's 5.8 and Love's 20.2 behind Allen's 18.3 — both projection calls, neither an override.

case.label: The numbers
case.body: 122.6 to 82.94 over Bok-aneers; best possible lineup 133.6 (week-6 archive, recomputed this run).

case.label: The lesson
case.body: Both were projection calls that lost. The fix is not to override — it is to set the lineup every week, which is done for Week 7: the lineup as set is the projection lineup.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: A Week 7 lineup set by projection leaves more than 15 points on the bench (archive).

waiverAnalysis.summary: The tool's weakest movable receiver is McLaurin — now confirmed season-ending — so four receivers clear the bar. Only Metcalf has a role reason that holds; the rest are vacancies or byes. Six weeks of data, still thin.
